recipes.snippet:
Go net/http (Go 1.22+). Runs a real query with a 2 s timeout on every call: 200 when the database answers, 503 when it does not, and nothing but the status word in the body (OPS-002: no versions, commit, dependency or engine names, no error text). `db` is your *sql.DB.
### file: health.go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"database/sql"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"time"
)

func healthHandler(db *sql.DB) http.HandlerFunc {
	return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), 2*time.Second)
		defer cancel()
		w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-store")
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		var one int
		if err := db.QueryRowContext(ctx, "SELECT 1").Scan(&one); err != nil {
			w.WriteHeader(http.StatusServiceUnavailable) // never echo err: it can carry hosts and versions
			_, _ = io.WriteString(w, `{"status":"unavailable"}`)
			return
		}
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, `{"status":"ok"}`)
	}
}
### file: main.go (register on the mux)
mux.HandleFunc("GET /healthz", healthHandler(db))
